subproblem.title: Derivative identities for a unit curve parametrized by its angle
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all vectors u, e ∈ ℝ^P, every real s and every γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ on (−s, s) and satisfies ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α), u⟩ > 0 and arctan(⟨γ(α), e⟩/⟨γ(α), u⟩) = α for every α ∈ (−s, s): for every α ∈ (−s, s), with γ′(α) := deriv γ α, ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0, ⟨γ(α),u⟩⟨γ′(α),e⟩ − ⟨γ(α),e⟩⟨γ′(α),u⟩ = ⟨γ(α),u⟩² + ⟨γ(α),e⟩², and γ′(α) ≠ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (u e : Euclid P) (s : ℝ) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Ioo (-s) s) → (∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, ‖γ α‖ = 1 ∧ 0 < inner ℝ (γ α) u ∧ Real.arctan (inner ℝ (γ α) e / inner ℝ (γ α) u) = α) → ∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, inner ℝ (γ α) (deriv γ α) = 0 ∧ inner ℝ (γ α) u * inner ℝ (deriv γ α) e - inner ℝ (γ α) e * inner ℝ (deriv γ α) u = inner ℝ (γ α) u ^ 2 + inner ℝ (γ α) e ^ 2 ∧ deriv γ α ≠ 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (|γ| ≡ 1 gives ⟨γ, γ′⟩ = 0; differentiating f(γ(α)) = α gives ⟨Aγ, γ′⟩ = |πγ|², so γ′ ≠ 0), stated for an arbitrary curve; orthonormality of u, e is not needed. Notation: I := (−s, s); ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product; γ′(α) := deriv γ α.
1. (Differentiability.) Fix α ∈ I. I is open, hence a neighbourhood of α. ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ I gives DifferentiableOn ℝ γ I (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0), so γ is differentiable at α and HasDerivAt γ (γ′(α)) α.
2. (Orthogonality.) n(β) := ⟨γ(β), γ(β)⟩ = ‖γ(β)‖² equals 1 for all β ∈ I, a neighbourhood of α, so n has derivative 0 at α. By the product rule for inner products (HasDerivAt.inner), n has derivative ⟨γ′(α), γ(α)⟩ + ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 2⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ at α. By uniqueness of derivatives, ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0.
3. (Derivative of the angle.) Let A(β) := ⟨γ(β), u⟩ and B(β) := ⟨γ(β), e⟩. By HasDerivAt.inner with a constant second argument they have derivatives A′ := ⟨γ′(α), u⟩ and B′ := ⟨γ′(α), e⟩ at α. Put x := A(α) > 0 and y := B(α). By the quotient rule (x ≠ 0), B/A has derivative (B′x − yA′)/x² at α, and by Real.hasDerivAt_arctan with the chain rule (HasDerivAt.arctan), h(β) := arctan(B(β)/A(β)) has derivative (1/(1 + (y/x)²))·(B′x − yA′)/x² = (B′x − yA′)/(x² + y²) at α, because (1 + (y/x)²)·x² = x² + y².
4. (Comparison.) By hypothesis h(β) = β for all β ∈ I, a neighbourhood of α, so h has derivative 1 at α (HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq with hasDerivAt_id). Hence (B′x − yA′)/(x² + y²) = 1, and since x² + y² ≥ x² > 0, xB′ − yA′ = x² + y², i.e. ⟨γ(α),u⟩⟨γ′(α),e⟩ − ⟨γ(α),e⟩⟨γ′(α),u⟩ = ⟨γ(α),u⟩² + ⟨γ(α),e⟩².
5. (Non-degeneracy.) The right-hand side in step 4 is ≥ x² > 0. If γ′(α) = 0, then A′ = B′ = 0 and the left-hand side would be 0. Hence γ′(α) ≠ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: γ is differentiable at every α ∈ (−s, s), being C¹ on an open interval.
Differentiating ‖γ‖² ≡ 1 gives ⟨γ, γ′⟩ = 0.
Differentiating arctan(B/A) ≡ α with A = ⟨γ,u⟩ > 0, B = ⟨γ,e⟩ gives A⟨γ′,e⟩ − B⟨γ′,u⟩ = A² + B² > 0, hence γ′ ≠ 0.

subproblem.title: Area formula for a piece of a cone over a unit curve
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, reals r₀, s with 0 < s < r₀, every γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ and injective on (−s, s) with ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0 and γ′(α) ≠ 0 for every α ∈ (−s, s), and every h : ℝ^P → ℝ: with R := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) × (−s, s) ⊆ ℝ × ℝ and S := {tγ(α) : (t, α) ∈ R}, the Bochner integral of h over S with respect to H² := μHE[2] equals the Lebesgue integral over R of t‖γ′(α)‖·h(tγ(α)) d(t, α).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (r₀ s : ℝ) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), 0 < s → s < r₀ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Ioo (-s) s) → InjOn γ (Ioo (-s) s) → (∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, ‖γ α‖ = 1 ∧ inner ℝ (γ α) (deriv γ α) = 0 ∧ deriv γ α ≠ 0) → ∫ x in (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) '' (Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s), h x ∂μHE[2] = ∫ q in Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s, q.1 * ‖deriv γ q.2‖ * h (q.1 • γ q.2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 9 (area formula for the parametrization G(t, α) = tγ(α) with Jacobian J_G = t|γ′|; Simon Ch. 2 §3). Conventions: J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s), R := J ×ˢ I ⊆ ℝ × ℝ with volume (the product Lebesgue measure); E₂ := Euclid 2 with coordinates w₀ := w 0, w₁ := w 1; γ′ := deriv γ. A Lean proof file may add the proof-only imports Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaParametrization (pinned SimonGMT package).
1. (Transport ℝ × ℝ ↔ Euclid 2.) Let Θ := (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ)).symm.trans MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow : E₂ ≃ᵐ ℝ × ℝ, so Θ(w) = (w₀, w₁). It is volume preserving: (EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin 2)).trans (volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ); and Θ.measurableEmbedding is a measurable embedding. Let R̃ := Θ⁻¹(R) = {w : w₀ ∈ J, w₁ ∈ I}, an open (hence measurable) set, and G̃ : E₂ → Euclid P, G̃(w) := w₀·γ(w₁). Then G̃ = G ∘ Θ with G(q) := q.1·γ(q.2), and since Θ is surjective, G̃(R̃) = G(Θ(Θ⁻¹ R)) = G(R) = S.
2. (Differentiability.) For w ∈ R̃, w₁ lies in the open interval I, so γ is differentiable at w₁ with derivative γ′(w₁) (ContDiffOn on an open set); the coordinate maps are continuous linear. By the product rule G̃ is differentiable at w and DG̃(w)h = h₀·γ(w₁) + w₀·h₁·γ′(w₁).
3. (Injective derivative.) Let w ∈ R̃ and suppose h₀·γ(w₁) + w₀h₁·γ′(w₁) = 0. Taking the inner product with γ(w₁) and using ⟨γ(w₁), γ(w₁)⟩ = 1 and ⟨γ(w₁), γ′(w₁)⟩ = 0 gives h₀ = 0; then w₀h₁·γ′(w₁) = 0 with w₀ > r₀ − s > 0 and γ′(w₁) ≠ 0 gives h₁ = 0. So DG̃(w) is injective.
4. (Injectivity.) If w, w′ ∈ R̃ and w₀·γ(w₁) = w′₀·γ(w′₁), taking norms (‖γ‖ = 1 on I; w₀, w′₀ > 0) gives w₀ = w′₀; dividing gives γ(w₁) = γ(w′₁), and injectivity of γ on I gives w₁ = w′₁. Hence w = w′, i.e. G̃ is injective on R̃.
5. (Area formula.) By SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean) with E := E₂, s := R̃ (measurable), f := G̃ (differentiable on R̃ with injective derivative, injective on R̃) and g := h: ∫_{G̃(R̃)} h dμHE[finrank ℝ E₂] = ∫_{R̃} areaJacobianAt G̃ w · h(G̃ w) dμHE[finrank ℝ E₂](w). On the source side μHE[finrank ℝ E₂] = volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); on the target side finrank ℝ E₂ = 2 (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so the left side is ∫_S h dμHE[2].
6. (Jacobian.) areaJacobianAt G̃ w = normDet(DG̃(w)) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), and normDet(L)² = det(Gram(L b₀, L b₁)) for the standard orthonormal basis b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 2) ℝ (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram), with normDet ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg). (Equivalently use areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_gram after reindexing the basis by Fin (finrank ℝ E₂).) Here DG̃(w)b₀ = γ(w₁) and DG̃(w)b₁ = w₀γ′(w₁), so the Gram matrix has diagonal entries ⟨γ(w₁), γ(w₁)⟩ = 1 and w₀²‖γ′(w₁)‖², and off-diagonal entries w₀⟨γ(w₁), γ′(w₁)⟩ = 0; its determinant is w₀²‖γ′(w₁)‖². Hence areaJacobianAt G̃ w = w₀‖γ′(w₁)‖ for w ∈ R̃ (w₀ > 0).
7. (Back to ℝ × ℝ.) By steps 5–6 and setIntegral_congr_fun on R̃, ∫_S h dμHE[2] = ∫_{R̃} Ψ(Θ w) dw with Ψ(q) := q.1‖γ′(q.2)‖·h(q.1·γ(q.2)). Since Θ is volume preserving with Θ⁻¹(R) = R̃, MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb (with Θ.measurableEmbedding) gives ∫_{R̃} Ψ(Θ w) dw = ∫_R Ψ(q) dq. This is the claimed identity; no integrability assumption is needed because every step is an equality of Bochner integrals. ∎
proof_key_steps: G̃(w) = w₀γ(w₁) on R̃ = Θ⁻¹(R) ⊆ Euclid 2 corresponds to G(t, α) = tγ(α) on R through the volume-preserving equivalence Θ : Euclid 2 ≃ᵐ ℝ × ℝ.
DG̃(w) = (γ(w₁), w₀γ′(w₁)) is injective (γ ⊥ γ′, γ′ ≠ 0, w₀ > 0) and G̃ is injective on R̃ (norms, injectivity of γ).
SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative with μHE[2] = volume on Euclid 2 turns ∫_S h dH² into ∫_{R̃} areaJacobianAt G̃ · h∘G̃.
The Gram determinant gives areaJacobianAt G̃ w = w₀‖γ′(w₁)‖; transport back to R ⊆ ℝ × ℝ with setIntegral_preimage_emb.

subproblem.title: du Bois-Reymond lemma on an open interval
subproblem.statement: For all reals a, b and every κ : ℝ → ℝ that is continuous on (a, b) such that ∫_ℝ φ′(x)κ(x) dx = 0 for every C¹ function φ : ℝ → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ (a, b): there is c ∈ ℝ with κ(x) = c for every x ∈ (a, b).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (a b : ℝ) (κ : ℝ → ℝ), ContinuousOn κ (Ioo a b) → (∀ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ Ioo a b → ∫ x, deriv φ x * κ x = 0) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo a b, κ x = c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 10, first sentence (κ has vanishing distributional derivative on (−s, s), hence is constant); this is the classical du Bois-Reymond lemma (Encyclopedia of Mathematics, "Du Bois-Reymond lemma"). The elementary argument below needs only the frozen imports; alternatively one may transport to Euclid 1 and use SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero (proof-only import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.DistributionalConstancy) followed by continuity. Notation: φ′ := deriv φ; 𝒟 := the set of C^∞ functions χ : ℝ → ℝ with compact support and tsupport χ ⊆ (a, b).
1. If b ≤ a, then (a, b) = ∅ and any c works. Assume a < b.
2. (Integrability.) For χ ∈ 𝒟, the function χ·κ vanishes outside the compact set K := tsupport χ ⊆ (a, b) and is continuous on K (κ is continuous on (a, b)); hence it is bounded and a.e.-strongly measurable (it equals the indicator of K times a function continuous on the measurable set K), so it is integrable.
3. (Normalized bump.) Let m := (a + b)/2 and let β be the ContDiffBump function centred at m with inner radius (b − a)/8 and outer radius (b − a)/4. Then β ∈ 𝒟, β ≥ 0, and β = 1 on [m − (b − a)/8, m + (b − a)/8], so I_β := ∫β > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg: β is nonnegative, integrable, and its support contains an interval of positive length). Put η := I_β⁻¹·β ∈ 𝒟, so ∫η = 1, and c := ∫η·κ.
4. (Antiderivatives.) Let χ ∈ 𝒟 and χ₀ := χ − (∫χ)·η. Then χ₀ is C^∞ with ∫χ₀ = 0; choose a < a′ < b′ < b with tsupport χ ∪ tsupport η ⊆ (a′, b′) (both are compact subsets of (a, b)), so χ₀ = 0 outside (a′, b′). Define Φ(x) := ∫_{a′}^{x} χ₀(y) dy. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right; χ₀ is continuous), Φ is differentiable with Φ′ = χ₀ everywhere, so Φ is C¹ (contDiff_one_iff_deriv). For x ≤ a′, χ₀ = 0 on [x, a′], so Φ(x) = 0; for x ≥ b′, Φ(x) = ∫_{a′}^{b′} χ₀ + ∫_{b′}^{x} χ₀ = ∫_ℝ χ₀ + 0 = 0. Hence support Φ ⊆ [a′, b′], so Φ has compact support and tsupport Φ ⊆ [a′, b′] ⊆ (a, b).
5. (Testing.) The hypothesis applied to Φ gives 0 = ∫Φ′κ = ∫χ₀κ = ∫χκ − (∫χ)(∫ηκ) (linearity; integrability from step 2). Hence ∫χ(x)(κ(x) − c) dx = 0 for every χ ∈ 𝒟.
6. (Fundamental lemma.) Suppose κ(x₀) ≠ c for some x₀ ∈ (a, b). Since the identity of step 5 also holds with κ − c replaced by c − κ, we may assume d := κ(x₀) − c > 0. By continuity of κ at x₀ (within the open interval) choose r > 0 with [x₀ − r, x₀ + r] ⊆ (a, b) and κ(x) − c > d/2 for |x − x₀| ≤ r. Let χ be the ContDiffBump function centred at x₀ with radii r/2 and r: χ ∈ 𝒟, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on [x₀ − r/2, x₀ + r/2], tsupport χ = [x₀ − r, x₀ + r]. Then χ(κ − c) ≥ 0 everywhere and χ(κ − c) ≥ d/2 on [x₀ − r/2, x₀ + r/2], so ∫χ(κ − c) ≥ r·d/2 > 0, contradicting step 5. Hence κ(x) = c for every x ∈ (a, b). ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix a normalized bump η ∈ C_c^∞(a, b) (a ContDiffBump divided by its positive integral) and c := ∫ηκ.
For χ ∈ C_c^∞(a, b), Φ(x) = ∫_{a′}^{x} (χ − (∫χ)η) is C¹ with compact support in (a, b) and Φ′ = χ − (∫χ)η.
Testing with Φ gives ∫χ(κ − c) = 0 for all χ ∈ C_c^∞(a, b).
A bump at a point where κ ≠ c contradicts this by continuity, so κ ≡ c on (a, b).

subproblem.title: Local inversion of a transversal C¹ map restricted to an embedded C¹ surface
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every embedded C¹ 2-dimensional submanifold M ⊆ ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 2 M), every p ∈ M, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P with p ∈ U and every map F : ℝ^P → ℝ² (Euclid 2) that is C¹ on U and whose derivative DF(p) is injective on Q := span(tangentSpace M p) (v ∈ Q and DF(p)v = 0 imply v = 0): there exist an open O ⊆ ℝ² with F(p) ∈ O, an open N ⊆ ℝ^P with p ∈ N ⊆ U, and G : ℝ² → ℝ^P that is C¹ on O, such that G(O) = M ∩ N, F(G(w)) = w for every w ∈ O, and tangentSpace M (G(w)) = range DG(w) for every w ∈ O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (p : Euclid P) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid 2), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 2 M → p ∈ M → IsOpen U → p ∈ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F U → (∀ v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M p), fderiv ℝ F p v = 0 → v = 0) → ∃ (O : Set (Euclid 2)) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P), IsOpen O ∧ IsOpen N ∧ F p ∈ O ∧ p ∈ N ∧ N ⊆ U ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G O ∧ G '' O = M ∩ N ∧ (∀ w ∈ O, F (G w) = w) ∧ ∀ w ∈ O, tangentSpace M (G w) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ G w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1, 4 and 5 (chart, inverse function theorem, relative openness of the image), stated for a general transversal C¹ map F instead of F = (|x|, f(x)). Conventions: E₂ := Euclid 2; B_r(x) := ball x r; Q := span(tangentSpace M p); "C¹" means ContDiff(On/At) ℝ 1; Dg := fderiv ℝ g. A Lean proof file may add the proof-only import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.ContDiff.
1. (Chart.) Apply IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 2 M at p: an open V₀ ⊆ E₂, an open W₀ ∋ p and ψ : E₂ → Euclid P that is C¹ on V₀, injective on V₀, with ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M, V₀ ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀, and Dψ(z) injective for z ∈ V₀. Choose v₀ ∈ V₀ with ψ(v₀) = p. By the accepted lemma Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (d := 2, r := 1, N := M), tangentSpace M (ψ v) = Set.range Dψ(v) for every v ∈ V₀; in particular Set.range Dψ(v₀) = tangentSpace M p ⊆ Q.
2. (Pointwise regularity.) As V₀ and U are open, ψ is C¹ at every v ∈ V₀ and F is C¹ at every x ∈ U (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt); in particular both are differentiable there with derivatives Dψ(v), DF(x).
3. (The composite.) V₀′ := V₀ ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) is open (ψ is continuous on the open set V₀; ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage) and contains v₀. Φ := F ∘ ψ is C¹ on V₀′ (composition), hence C¹ at v₀ with DΦ(v₀) = DF(p) ∘ Dψ(v₀) (chain rule). DΦ(v₀) : E₂ → E₂ is injective: if DF(p)(Dψ(v₀)z) = 0, then Dψ(v₀)z ∈ tangentSpace M p ⊆ Q, so transversality gives Dψ(v₀)z = 0, and injectivity of Dψ(v₀) gives z = 0. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space E₂ is bijective, so DΦ(v₀) is the coercion of a continuous linear equivalence E₀ : E₂ ≃L[ℝ] E₂ (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, then LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv).
4. (Invertibility persists.) v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous on the open set V₀′ (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), and the set of continuous linear maps that are coercions of continuous linear equivalences is open (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen). Hence V₁′ := {v ∈ V₀′ : DΦ(v) is such a coercion} is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage) and contains v₀.
5. (Inverse function theorem.) Φ is C¹ at v₀ with HasFDerivAt Φ E₀ v₀, so ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph (n = 1 ≠ 0) yields an open partial homeomorphism Φ̃ whose coercion is Φ and with v₀ ∈ Φ̃.source. Restrict it to the open set V₁′ (OpenPartialHomeomorph.restrOpen, source = Φ̃.source ∩ V₁′): this gives Φ₁ with open source V₁ ∋ v₀ (so V₁ ⊆ V₀, ψ(V₁) ⊆ U, and DΦ(v) is invertible for every v ∈ V₁) and open target O := Φ₁.target = Φ(V₁). Then Φ₁.symm maps O into V₁, Φ(Φ₁.symm w) = w for w ∈ O, Φ₁.symm(O) = V₁ (symm_image_target_eq_source), and F(p) = Φ(v₀) ∈ O.
6. (C¹ inverse.) Let w ∈ O, v := Φ₁.symm w ∈ V₁, and let E_v be the equivalence with DΦ(v) = E_v. Φ is C¹ at v with HasFDerivAt Φ E_v v, so OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm (w ∈ Φ₁.target) shows that Φ₁.symm is C¹ at w, and OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm gives HasFDerivAt Φ₁.symm E_v⁻¹ w; E_v⁻¹ is surjective.
7. (Definition of G.) Put G := ψ ∘ Φ₁.symm. For w ∈ O, ψ is C¹ at Φ₁.symm w ∈ V₀ and Φ₁.symm is C¹ at w, so G is C¹ at w; hence G is C¹ on O. F(G w) = (F ∘ ψ)(Φ₁.symm w) = Φ(Φ₁.symm w) = w. By the chain rule DG(w) = Dψ(v) ∘ E_v⁻¹ with v = Φ₁.symm w; since E_v⁻¹ is surjective, Set.range DG(w) = Set.range Dψ(v) = tangentSpace M (ψ v) = tangentSpace M (G w) by step 1. Finally G(O) = ψ(Φ₁.symm(O)) = ψ(V₁).
8. (ψ(V₁) is relatively open in M.) For each v ∈ V₁ choose ε_v > 0 with B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁, and, by the accepted lemma Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity (applied to V₀, W₀, ψ: ψ is continuous and injective on V₀, ψ(V₀) ⊆ W₀, and the properness of step 1), choose δ_v > 0 such that every v′ ∈ V₀ with ‖ψ(v′) − ψ(v)‖ < δ_v satisfies ‖v′ − v‖ < ε_v. Let N₀ := ⋃_{v ∈ V₁} (W₀ ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v)), an open set. Then M ∩ N₀ = ψ(V₁): if x ∈ M ∩ W₀ ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v), then x ∈ W₀ ∩ M = ψ(V₀), say x = ψ(v′) with v′ ∈ V₀, and ‖ψ(v′) − ψ(v)‖ < δ_v forces v′ ∈ B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁, so x ∈ ψ(V₁); conversely, for v ∈ V₁, ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V₀) = W₀ ∩ M and ψ(v) ∈ B_{δ_v}(ψ v).
9. (Conclusion.) Put N := N₀ ∩ U, an open subset of U. Since ψ(V₁) ⊆ U, M ∩ N = (M ∩ N₀) ∩ U = ψ(V₁) ∩ U = ψ(V₁) = G(O). As v₀ ∈ V₁, p = ψ(v₀) ∈ M ∩ N, so p ∈ N. Hence O, N are open, F(p) ∈ O, p ∈ N ⊆ U, G is C¹ on O, G(O) = M ∩ N, and F(G w) = w and tangentSpace M (G w) = Set.range DG(w) for every w ∈ O. ∎

subproblem.title: The tangent plane of a locally radially invariant C¹ surface at p is 2-dimensional and contains p
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every M ⊆ ℝ^P that is an embedded C¹ 2-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 2 M), every p ∈ M and every ρ > 0 such that t·x ∈ M whenever x ∈ M ∩ B_ρ(p), t > 0 and t·x ∈ B_ρ(p): the linear span Q := span(tangentSpace M p) has dimension 2 and p ∈ Q.

1. (Chart.) Since p ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = p.
2. (finrank Q = 2.) By the accepted lemma Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (with P, d := 2, r := 1, N := M, W, V, ψ, v := v₀; its hypotheses are 1 ≤ 1 and exactly the chart properties of step 1), tangentSpace M p = tangentSpace M (ψ v₀) = Set.range L with L := fderiv ℝ ψ v₀ : Euclid 2 →L[ℝ] Euclid P. Set.range L is the carrier of the submodule LinearMap.range L, so Q = LinearMap.range L (Submodule.span_eq). L is injective, hence finrank Q = finrank (Euclid 2) = 2 (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
3. (Trivial case.) If p = 0, then p ∈ Q because Q is a submodule. Assume from now on p ≠ 0, so ‖p‖ > 0, and put ε₀ := min(1/2, ρ/(2‖p‖)) > 0.
4. (Radial curve.) Define c : ℝ → Euclid P, c(t) := (1 + ε₀t)·p. It is affine, hence ContDiff (in particular C¹ on (−1, 1)); c(0) = p; and c has derivative ε₀·p at 0 (t ↦ 1 + ε₀t has derivative ε₀; HasDerivAt.smul_const).

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4–5 and the definition of tangentSpace (witness curve c), ε₀·p ∈ tangentSpace M p ⊆ Q (Submodule.subset_span). As ε₀ ≠ 0, p = ε₀⁻¹·(ε₀·p) ∈ Q (Submodule.smul_mem). Together with step 2: finrank Q = 2 and p ∈ Q. ∎

For p ≠ 0 the affine curve c(t) = (1 + ε₀t)p with ε₀ = min(1/2, ρ/(2‖p‖)) stays in B_ρ(p) and, by radial invariance applied at x = p, in M.
Hence ε₀p = c′(0) ∈ tangentSpace M p, so p ∈ span(tangentSpace M p) (trivially also when p = 0).

subproblem.title: Local cone structure of a radially invariant C¹ surface near p = r₀u
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every embedded C¹ 2-dimensional submanifold M ⊆ ℝ^P, every unit vector u ∈ ℝ^P, every r₀ > 0 with r₀u ∈ M and every ρ > 0 such that t·x ∈ M whenever x ∈ M ∩ B_ρ(r₀u), t > 0 and t·x ∈ B_ρ(r₀u): there exist a unit vector e with ⟨u, e⟩ = 0, a real s with 0 < s < r₀, an open N ⊆ ℝ^P with r₀u ∈ N ⊆ B_ρ(r₀u) and ⟨x, u⟩ > 0 for all x ∈ N, and γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ on (−s, s) with γ(0) = u and γ′(0) = e, such that ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α), u⟩ > 0 and arctan(⟨γ(α),e⟩/⟨γ(α),u⟩) = α for every α ∈ (−s, s); M ∩ N = {tγ(α) : t ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), α ∈ (−s, s)}; and span(tangentSpace M (tγ(α))) = span{γ(α), γ′(α)} for all t ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) and α ∈ (−s, s).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (u : Euclid P) (r₀ ρ : ℝ), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 2 M → ‖u‖ = 1 → 0 < r₀ → r₀ • u ∈ M → 0 < ρ → (∀ x ∈ M ∩ ball (r₀ • u) ρ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → t • x ∈ ball (r₀ • u) ρ → t • x ∈ M) → ∃ (e : Euclid P) (s : ℝ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P), ‖e‖ = 1 ∧ inner ℝ u e = 0 ∧ 0 < s ∧ s < r₀ ∧ IsOpen N ∧ r₀ • u ∈ N ∧ N ⊆ ball (r₀ • u) ρ ∧ (∀ x ∈ N, 0 < inner ℝ x u) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Ioo (-s) s) ∧ γ 0 = u ∧ deriv γ 0 = e ∧ (∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, ‖γ α‖ = 1 ∧ 0 < inner ℝ (γ α) u ∧ Real.arctan (inner ℝ (γ α) e / inner ℝ (γ α) u) = α) ∧ M ∩ N = (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) '' (Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s), ∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M (t • γ α)) = Submodule.span ℝ {γ α, deriv γ α}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1–6 (chart, p ∈ Q, coordinates u, e, f, F, inverse function theorem, relative openness, radial structure), with p := r₀u. Conventions: B_r(x) := ball x r; ⟨·,·⟩ real inner product; p := r₀u; Q := span(tangentSpace M p); J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s); g′ := deriv g, Dg := fderiv ℝ g; for t, α ∈ ℝ, ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ denotes the point of Euclid 2 with coordinates (t, α) (Lean: !₂[t, α]). Note ⟨p, u⟩ = r₀‖u‖² = r₀ and ‖p‖ = r₀.
1. (The plane Q.) Sibling idtp_ccd_scsp_tangent_plane_mem applied to (P, M, p, ρ) (its hypotheses: M is an embedded C¹ 2-submanifold, p = r₀u ∈ M, ρ > 0, and the radial hypothesis) gives finrank Q = 2 and p ∈ Q; hence u = r₀⁻¹p ∈ Q.
2. (Choice of e.) span{u} ≤ Q and finrank span{u} = 1 < 2 = finrank Q (finrank_span_singleton), so span{u} < Q and there is w ∈ Q with w ∉ span{u} (SetLike.exists_of_lt). Then e′ := w − ⟨w,u⟩u ∈ Q, e′ ≠ 0 (otherwise w = ⟨w,u⟩u ∈ span{u}) and ⟨u, e′⟩ = ⟨u,w⟩ − ⟨w,u⟩‖u‖² = 0. Put e := ‖e′‖⁻¹e′; then e ∈ Q, ‖e‖ = 1, ⟨u, e⟩ = 0. (u, e) is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so span{u, e} has finrank 2; since span{u, e} ≤ Q and finrank Q = 2, Q = span{u, e} (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). Consequently every v ∈ Q satisfies v = ⟨v,u⟩u + ⟨v,e⟩e (write v = a·u + b·e by Submodule.mem_span_pair and take inner products with u and e).
3. (Coordinates.) Let ρ₁ := min(ρ, r₀/2) > 0 and U := B_{ρ₁}(p), an open set with p ∈ U ⊆ B_ρ(p). For x ∈ U, ⟨x,u⟩ = ⟨p,u⟩ + ⟨x − p, u⟩ ≥ r₀ − ‖x − p‖ > r₀/2 > 0; in particular x ≠ 0. Define f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩) and F : Euclid P → Euclid 2, F(x) := ⟨⟨‖x‖, f(x)⟩⟩. On U both coordinate functions are C^∞: the norm is smooth away from 0 (contDiffAt_norm), x ↦ ⟨x,e⟩ and x ↦ ⟨x,u⟩ are continuous linear, the quotient is smooth where ⟨x,u⟩ ≠ 0, and arctan is smooth (Real.contDiff_arctan); hence F is C¹ on U (coordinatewise criterion contDiffOn_piLp). Homogeneity: if ⟨x,u⟩ > 0 and c > 0 then f(c·x) = arctan(c⟨x,e⟩/(c⟨x,u⟩)) = f(x) and ‖c·x‖ = c‖x‖. Values at p: ⟨p,e⟩ = r₀⟨u,e⟩ = 0, so f(p) = arctan 0 = 0 and F(p) = ⟨⟨r₀, 0⟩⟩. Derivative at p, coordinatewise (hasStrictFDerivAt_piLp / hasFDerivWithinAt_piLp): the norm has derivative h ↦ ⟨p, h⟩/‖p‖ = ⟨u, h⟩ at p ≠ 0 (e.g. from (hasFDerivAt_id p).norm_sq and HasFDerivAt.sqrt, using Real.sqrt_sq), and Df(p)h = (1/(1 + 0²))·(⟨h,e⟩⟨p,u⟩ − ⟨p,e⟩⟨h,u⟩)/⟨p,u⟩² = ⟨e, h⟩/r₀. So DF(p)h = ⟨⟨⟨u, h⟩, ⟨e, h⟩/r₀⟩⟩.
4. (Transversality.) If v ∈ Q and DF(p)v = 0, then ⟨u,v⟩ = 0 and ⟨e,v⟩ = 0, so v = ⟨v,u⟩u + ⟨v,e⟩e = 0 by step 2. Hence DF(p) is injective on Q.
5. (Local inverse.) Sibling idtp_ccd_scsp_local_inverse applied to (P, M, p, U, F) gives an open O ⊆ Euclid 2, an open N₀ ⊆ Euclid P and G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P with F(p) ∈ O, p ∈ N₀ ⊆ U, G C¹ on O, G(O) = M ∩ N₀, F(G w) = w for w ∈ O, and tangentSpace M (G w) = Set.range DG(w) for w ∈ O. If x ∈ M ∩ N₀, then x = G w for some w ∈ O, so F x = w and G(F x) = x.
6. (Square and the set N.) As O is open and F(p) = ⟨⟨r₀, 0⟩⟩ ∈ O, choose ε > 0 with B_ε(F p) ⊆ O and fix s with 0 < s < min(ε/2, r₀/2). Let R_s := {w ∈ Euclid 2 : |w₀ − r₀| < s and |w₁| < s} = {⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ : t ∈ J, α ∈ I} (w₀, w₁ the coordinates of w), an open set. For w ∈ R_s, ‖w − F p‖² = (w₀ − r₀)² + w₁² < 2s² < ε², so R_s ⊆ B_ε(F p) ⊆ O; also 0 < s < r₀. Define N := N₀ ∩ (U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s)); since F is continuous on the open set U, U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage), so N is open. N ⊆ N₀ ⊆ U ⊆ B_ρ(p), and ⟨x, u⟩ > 0 for every x ∈ N (step 3). p ∈ N because p ∈ N₀, p ∈ U and F(p) ∈ R_s. Claim: M ∩ N = G(R_s). If x ∈ M ∩ N, then x ∈ M ∩ N₀, so x = G(F x) with F x ∈ R_s. Conversely, if w ∈ R_s ⊆ O, then G w ∈ G(O) = M ∩ N₀, so G w ∈ M and G w ∈ N₀ ⊆ U, and F(G w) = w ∈ R_s; hence G w ∈ M ∩ N.
7. (The curve.) Define γ(α) := r₀⁻¹·G(⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩). The map α ↦ ⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩ is affine and maps I into R_s ⊆ O, so γ is C¹ on I (ContDiffOn.comp, then multiplication by a constant). For α ∈ I put x_α := G(⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩) ∈ G(R_s) = M ∩ N; then F(x_α) = ⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩, i.e. ‖x_α‖ = r₀ and f(x_α) = α. Hence ‖γ(α)‖ = 1; x_α ∈ N gives ⟨x_α, u⟩ > 0, so ⟨γ(α), u⟩ = r₀⁻¹⟨x_α, u⟩ > 0; and by homogeneity f(γ(α)) = f(x_α) = α, i.e. arctan(⟨γ(α),e⟩/⟨γ(α),u⟩) = α. Also γ(0) = r₀⁻¹·G(F p) = r₀⁻¹·p = u, using p ∈ M ∩ N₀ and step 5.
8. (Radial structure.) Claim: G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) = t·γ(α) for all t ∈ J and α ∈ I. Fix α ∈ I and let A := {t ∈ J : G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) = t·γ(α)}. (i) r₀ ∈ A, since r₀·γ(α) = G(⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩). (ii) closure(A) ∩ J ⊆ A: the maps t ↦ G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) and t ↦ t·γ(α) are continuous on the open interval J (G is continuous on O and t ↦ ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ maps J into R_s), so their equalizer is relatively closed in J. (iii) A is open: let t ∈ A and x := t·γ(α) = G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) ∈ M ∩ N. As N is open, choose η > 0 with B_η(x) ⊆ N and η ≤ t − (r₀ − s). Let |t′ − t| < η; then t′ > r₀ − s > 0 and ‖t′·γ(α) − x‖ = |t′ − t|·‖γ(α)‖ < η, so y := t′·γ(α) ∈ N ⊆ B_ρ(p). Moreover y = (t′/t)·x with x ∈ M ∩ B_ρ(p) (as N ⊆ B_ρ(p)) and t′/t > 0, so y ∈ M by the radial hypothesis. Thus y ∈ M ∩ N = G(R_s), say y = G(w) with w ∈ R_s, and then w = F(G w) = F(y) = ⟨⟨‖t′·γ(α)‖, f(t′·γ(α))⟩⟩ = ⟨⟨t′, f(γ(α))⟩⟩ = ⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩, using t′ > 0, ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α), u⟩ > 0 and homogeneity. Hence ⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩ = w ∈ R_s, i.e. t′ ∈ J, and G(⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩) = y = t′·γ(α), i.e. t′ ∈ A. So (t − η, t + η) ⊆ A. (iv) J is preconnected, A is open, A ∩ J ≠ ∅ and closure(A) ∩ J ⊆ A, so J ⊆ A (IsPreconnected.subset_of_closure_inter_subset). Consequently M ∩ N = G(R_s) = {t·γ(α) : t ∈ J, α ∈ I}, i.e. M ∩ N is the image of J ×ˢ I under q ↦ q.1·γ(q.2).
9. (Tangent planes.) Let t ∈ J, α ∈ I, w := ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ ∈ R_s and x := t·γ(α) = G w. G agrees with G̃(w′) := w′₀·γ(w′₁) on the open neighbourhood R_s of w (step 8), so DG(w) = DG̃(w) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Since γ is differentiable at α (I is open), G̃ is differentiable at w with DG̃(w)h = h₀·γ(α) + t·h₁·γ′(α) (product rule). As t ≠ 0, Set.range DG̃(w) = {c₁γ(α) + c₂γ′(α) : c₁, c₂ ∈ ℝ}, the carrier of span{γ(α), γ′(α)} (Submodule.mem_span_pair). By step 5, tangentSpace M x = Set.range DG(w) is the carrier of span{γ(α), γ′(α)}; therefore span(tangentSpace M (t·γ(α))) = span{γ(α), γ′(α)} (Submodule.span_eq).
10. (γ′(0) = e.) Sibling idtp_ccd_scsp_angle_curve applied to (P, u, e, s, γ) (hypotheses from step 7) at α = 0, where γ(0) = u, gives ⟨u, γ′(0)⟩ = 0 and ⟨u,u⟩⟨γ′(0),e⟩ − ⟨u,e⟩⟨γ′(0),u⟩ = ⟨u,u⟩² + ⟨u,e⟩²; since ⟨u,u⟩ = 1 and ⟨u,e⟩ = 0, this says ⟨γ′(0), e⟩ = 1. By step 9 with t = r₀, α = 0 (r₀·γ(0) = p), Q = span(tangentSpace M p) = span{u, γ′(0)} ∋ γ′(0), and by step 2, γ′(0) = ⟨γ′(0),u⟩u + ⟨γ′(0),e⟩e = 0·u + 1·e = e.
11. (Collect.) The data e, s, N, γ satisfy: ‖e‖ = 1 and ⟨u, e⟩ = 0 (step 2); 0 < s < r₀ (step 6); N open, r₀u = p ∈ N, N ⊆ B_ρ(r₀u) and ⟨x, u⟩ > 0 on N (step 6); γ C¹ on I with γ(0) = u (step 7) and γ′(0) = e (step 10); ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α),u⟩ > 0 and arctan(⟨γ(α),e⟩/⟨γ(α),u⟩) = α on I (step 7); M ∩ N = image of J ×ˢ I under q ↦ q.1·γ(q.2) (step 8); and span(tangentSpace M (t·γ(α))) = span{γ(α), γ′(α)} for t ∈ J, α ∈ I (step 9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Sibling tangent_plane_mem: Q = span(tangentSpace M p), p = r₀u, has finrank 2 and contains u; choose a unit e ∈ Q with ⟨u,e⟩ = 0, so Q = span{u, e}.
F(x) = (‖x‖, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩)) is C¹ on U = B_{min(ρ, r₀/2)}(p) ⊆ {⟨x,u⟩ > 0}, and DF(p)v = (⟨u,v⟩, ⟨e,v⟩/r₀) is injective on Q.
Sibling local_inverse gives O, N₀, G with G(O) = M ∩ N₀ and F∘G = id on O; shrinking to a square R_s ⊆ O and N := N₀ ∩ U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s) gives M ∩ N = G(R_s).
γ(α) := r₀⁻¹G(r₀, α) satisfies ‖γ‖ = 1, ⟨γ,u⟩ > 0, f(γ(α)) = α, γ(0) = u; radial invariance, F∘G = id and connectedness of (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) give G(t, α) = tγ(α).
range DG(t, α) = span{γ(α), γ′(α)} gives the tangent planes; sibling angle_curve and γ′(0) ∈ Q = span{u, e} give γ′(0) = e.
